layout.title: How a microwave works

shows.does: a hand presses start and violet waves shine down on a cold mug
one side of the mug glows hot while the rest stays cold blue
the turntable spins the mug through the waves and it warms all round
violet waves leak out of the open front
a door with a metal mesh closes the front and the leaking waves stop
a ring traced round the mesh door
the door swings open mid-cook and waves leak toward the hand
a red latch switch appears, the door shuts and the waves cut out
the magnetron runs again and glows red hot
a fan appears and blows cool air across the magnetron
the mug keeps cooking and boils over in a spill of steam
a timer counts down and the waves switch off
the hand presses start, the light comes on and the mug steams
the microwave running with a steaming mug

layout.why: A microwave oven stands cut open on a cart in a kitchen with a cold mug on its turntable and a hand at its start button; the waves are followed from the magnetron into the cavity, onto the mug and out at the door, and the heat they leave in the magnetron to its fan. The camera opens close on the mug under the waves, frames each part as it is added, and ends on the hand pressing start and the mug steaming.

sentences.text: If you aim invisible waves at a cold mug, you have a microwave.
But the waves bounce into hot spots, and half stays cold.
So a turntable spins the mug through the spots.
But now the waves leak out the open front.
So a door with metal mesh blocks them.
But open that door mid-cook, and waves hit your hand.
So a switch in the latch cuts the power.
But now the hard-working magnetron gets burning hot.
So a fan blows cool air across it.
But now the mug keeps cooking until it boils over.
So a timer switches the waves off.
Press start, and your mug comes out steaming.

recurring.what: a hand at the start button
